title: promotion-fast-forward: the explicit fetch refspec is never asserted in the accept direction, and every refspec mutant dies only in one test about a different property
description:
Routed by opum-agent 2026-09-15: opum-doc measured that in their reference SHELL implementation the drop-refspec mutant SURVIVES the corrected fixture with 0 red, because the earlier missing-ref split emits the same diagnosis and exit code the shallow row asserts. lore-cli found the equivalent in its own .mjs -- deleting the workflow fetch line survived, and one wiring assertion fixed it. They asked this repository to confirm which mutant dies here and record it.

MEASURED HERE, and the honest answer is in between: the mutants DO die, and they die for the wrong reason.

Two mutants against scripts/qualification/promotion-fast-forward.mjs, each run over the whole of test/qcli314-promotion-fast-forward.test.ts:
  A  refspec +refs/heads/dev:refs/remotes/origin/dev  -->  bare "dev"        13 pass, 1 fail
  B  refspec dropped entirely (git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin)           13 pass, 1 fail

BOTH KILL THE SAME SINGLE TEST, and it is "a remote with no dev blames the REMOTE and quotes git own error" -- a test about DIAGNOSIS ATTRIBUTION, not about fetch wiring. It dies incidentally, and differently in each case:
  A  git raw message becomes "couldn not find remote ref dev" instead of "... refs/heads/dev", so the assertion quoting git own text misses. The test is coupled to the refspec only because the refspec happens to appear inside the string git prints.
  B  a bare git fetch origin SUCCEEDS against a remote that has no dev, so the REMOTE-blaming branch never executes at all and the run falls through to the missing-ref split.

So selective redness here is real but it is not evidence the refspec is under test. Nothing asserts the property the refspec exists for.

WHY THE OBVIOUS CANDIDATE CANNOT COVER IT. The suite already has "a missing origin/dev in a SHALLOW clone blames the workflow, not the remote". That test builds the shallow fixture and then REMOVES THE REMOTE (git remote remove origin) with the comment that this reproduces the no-refspec outcome without mutating the script. That is true for the diagnosis, and it makes the test structurally blind to a refspec mutant: with no remote, the fetch never runs, so no mutation of the fetch line can change the result. The test cannot fail for this reason by construction.

THE PROPERTY THAT IS MISSING IS THE ACCEPT DIRECTION. The refspec exists so that origin/dev comes into existence as a consequence of THIS SCRIPT rather than of a clone configuration nobody controls from the workflow. Measured against the production shape -- git clone --depth 1 --branch main, remote INTACT, is-shallow true, remote.origin.fetch covering only main, origin/dev absent:
  original, explicit refspec   exit 0, verdict emitted, and refs/remotes/origin/dev EXISTS after the run
  mutant A                     exit 1, shallow diagnosis
  mutant B                     exit 1, shallow diagnosis
The two mutants produce byte-identical output to each other, and that output is exactly what the existing shallow test already asserts -- which is the shape opum-doc reported. What separates the original from both mutants is not a better error, it is that the original SUCCEEDS.

This is the fleet rule in CLAUDE.md landing on its own guard: proving a gate rejects is half the proof and proving it accepts is the other half. QCLI-314 proved this file rejects, thoroughly and in many shapes. The one thing the refspec line does is make an accept POSSIBLE in a clone that would otherwise fail, and the accept direction is where it was never measured.

The fix is one test, not a redesign: keep the remote, assert exit 0 and the created ref.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test builds the production-shape fixture -- a shallow clone cut as git clone --depth 1 --branch main with the remote LEFT INTACT -- and asserts the run is ACCEPTED (exit 0, verdict on stdout) and that refs/remotes/origin/dev exists afterwards, so the refspec job is measured in the accept direction rather than through a diagnosis string

Both refspec mutants (bare dev, and no refspec at all) are run against the new test and both turn it RED, recorded as two named runs with their exit codes and messages; the rest of the suite verdicts are unchanged by the addition
The record states which test killed each mutant BEFORE this change and why that coupling was incidental, and why the existing shallow no-dev test is structurally incapable of covering the refspec

plan: 1. Add a production-shape fixture helper: git clone --depth 1 --branch main from the scratch origin, remote left INTACT, asserting the preconditions (is-shallow true, remote.origin.fetch covering only main, origin/dev absent) so the fixture cannot silently stop being the shape under test

2. Assert the ACCEPT direction: BEFORE_SHA=ZERO (branch creation is the one accept path a depth-1 clone can reach, since any real previous HEAD is unfetchable there), exit 0, the verdict on stdout, and refs/remotes/origin/dev resolving afterwards
3. Run both refspec mutants against the new test and record both reds with their messages
4. Restore, run the full file plus the full suite, open a PR
